summary: This article explains how sinkholes form when rock underground slowly dissolves and the ground above suddenly or slowly sinks, and why some parts of Saudi Arabia must watch for them.
introduce: Read the title “Sinkholes: When the Ground Collapses” aloud and ask each student to write one question they hope the article will answer. Collect a few questions, then explain that today they will find the one big idea that ties all the details together.

keyTerms.def: a type of soft rock that can slowly dissolve in water
to slowly break apart and mix into a liquid
a hollow, empty space inside something solid

challengeTerms.def: a landscape shaped by large amounts of limestone that slowly dissolves underground
the slow wearing away of rock or soil, often by water
a low, sunken area in the ground's surface

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that the ground under your feet can feel solid even when it is secretly hollow underneath? Use evidence from the article to explain.
Explain why pumping too much groundwater can make a sinkhole more likely in some places.
struggling: Pre-teach limestone, dissolve, and cavity with pictures or gestures, then let weak readers complete a main-idea-and-details web with a partner.
gifted: Challenge advanced readers to use karst, erosion, and depression in a short paragraph that states the main idea of the article in their own words.
